title: Operational runway tilt for quantization adoption and staffing
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet ties a short-term headcount plan to an operational cost model expressed as a runway tilt driven by quantization adoption across our inference fleet. The goal is to produce an actionable set of levers (hiring, commit levels, token price adjustments) that extend runway by 6–12 months under three realistic demand trajectories while preserving SLA margins for Dedicated customers.

Executive summary (high level):
- If quantization profiles (int8/int4 + kernel tuning) are rolled to 50% of production traffic, total GPU inference cost per 1M tokens falls ~18–24% depending on model mix.
- Primary tradeoffs: engineering ramp (3 FTE infra engineers + 1 applied-ML) vs. immediate price changes. Upfront hiring increases opex but unlocks sustained unit cost improvements.
- We recommend a staged path: pilot (Q1) -> scale (Q2) -> bind to SLA contracts (Q3). If customer demand grows >30% q/q, trigger an urgent dedicated capacity add; otherwise, defer hires to Q2.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline token demand: 120B tokens/month (mixed hosted + dedicated).
- Baseline effective GPU cost (spot blended): $0.68 / 1k tokens at current kernel mix.
- Quantization adoption effectiveness bands: conservative (10% cost reduction), expected (20%), aggressive (28%).
- Engineering productivity and ramp: new infra hire achieves full quantization rollout contribution in 12 weeks; applied-ML role in 8 weeks.
- Hiring incremental fully-burdened monthly cost: infra FTE $28k, applied-ML $34k, SRE $24k.
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) discount tiers: 0% (on-demand), 15% (quarter commit), 28% (annual commit).

Scenarios (textual table):
- Scenario A: Low growth (0–5% q/q). Adopt expected quantization (20%). Delay adding infra hires until Q2. Net unit cost reduction: ~20%. Runway extension (months): +8 months vs baseline. No change to pricing.
- Scenario B: Medium growth (15–25% q/q). Fast-path hires (2 infra, 1 applied-ML) in Q1. Adopt expected->aggressive quantization (ramped to 40–60% traffic) by Q3. Net unit cost reduction: 22–25% after Q3. Recommend offering a limited early-bird committed Dedicated SKU with a 20% price uplift for higher SLOs. Runway extension: +6 months but short-term opex spike.
- Scenario C: High growth (>35% q/q). Immediate hiring (3 infra, 1 applied-ML, 2 SRE) and increased reserved capacity commits to lock price. Net effective unit cost drop ~26–28% but opex increases substantially month 1–4. Consider modest token price increase (5–8%) for new high-throughput accounts. Runway effect: neutral-to-positive depending on price uplift.

Quantization sensitivity sweep (narrative):
- For each incremental 5% of traffic moved to quantized kernels we see diminishing returns: first 30% traffic yields the bulk of savings (approx 18–22%), next 20% yields smaller marginal gains (3–6%). The marginal cost of moving traffic is primarily engineering time and validation SLAs for outputs.

Headcount plan (practical cadence):
- Option 1 (cost-conservative): Hire 1 infra (Q2), 1 applied-ML (Q2). Delay SRE until Q4.
- Option 2 (balanced): Hire 2 infra, 1 applied-ML, 1 SRE (Q1). Use a 16-week ramp for infra.
- Option 3 (aggressive): Hire 3 infra, 2 applied-ML, 2 SRE (immediate). Budget this as a special 3-month runway acceleration.

Budget impact by month (narrative numbers):
- Baseline monthly opex for inference fleet: $2.1M (infra + cloud + licenses + operator costs).
- Hiring Option 2 incremental monthly burden (after hires live): ~+$140k/month run rate.
- Expected steady-state cost reduction from quantization (Option 2 at scale): ~$420k/month saved at 20% token take to quantized kernels. Payback period for hires: ~10–12 months (conservative).

Pricing sensitivity (textual stress test):
- If unit token price is reduced by 10% to stimulate demand, our model predicts demand elasticity between 0.15–0.35 in the first 6 months (low-medium). Under elastic=0.25, tokens increase ~10–12%, which offsets ~75% of the immediate revenue drop; net revenue falls ~2–3% while utilization and longer-term adoption rises.
- If price increases by 8% to protect margin under high-demand scenario, churn risk exists only for price-sensitive small accounts; enterprise/top-10 accounts show inelastic behavior (0.02–0.08 elasticity) and expected retention.

Operational triggers (decision rules):
- Trigger A (hire): 3-month rolling token growth >20% w/o proportional commit revenue -> approve Option 2 hiring.
- Trigger B (price promo): If dedicated commit uptake < forecast for two consecutive months, run a targeted 8-week limited discount campaign tied to minimum commit.
- Trigger C (defer hires): If quantization pilot (two-week A/B) fails to show >10% unit cost reduction or introduces output quality regressions above our threshold, pause hires and revert to conservative barrier.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Quantization introduces unacceptable regression on structured outputs. Mitigation: holdback 20% of critical enterprise traffic on calibrated float paths and run regressions per prompt set; add rollback quick-path in runtime.
- Risk: Hiring delays mean we miss commit discounts window. Mitigation: temporary contractor bridge for infra tasks and negotiate flexible reserved capacity windows with cloud partners.
- Risk: Elastic demand overshoots capacity causing latency SLO misses. Mitigation: pre-authorize limited burst pool and implement automatic fallback to a slightly higher-cost model variant.

Next actions (concrete):
1) Launch a 6-week quantization pilot covering 10% of mixed traffic (scope: two popular models). Owner: Applied ML (Lena Cho). Start: 2026-01-18.
2) Prepare a constrained hiring requisition for Option 2 for finance approval by 2026-01-25. Owner: Finance (Aisha R. Patel).
3) Build monitoring dashboards for unit cost by model, kernel, and commit level. Owner: Observability (Marco Gutierrez). ETA: 2026-02-08.
4) Draft a customer communication template for potential minor price adjustments and commit offers. Owner: GTM finance liaison.

Appendix (quick sensitivity bullets):
- Breakeven token uplift needed to sustain a 10% price cut (elasticity=0.25): ~30% token increase over 6 months.
- Breakeven for hiring Option 2 (assuming 20% quant gains): ~11 months.
- Worst-case short term (no quant gains + hires): runway reduction by ~2 months; contingency: pause non-critical hires and tighten contract windows.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working spreadsheet narrative. the embedded numeric model (sheet tabs) will include month-by-month cashflow, hire ramp profile, and per-model token unit economics. please comment on the triggers and any alternative trigger thresholds you prefer (e.g., 15% growth threshold instead of 20%).
